utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We have a new witness. Can the usher please assist? Please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, counsel, Mr. Pisarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Pisarevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have already had the redacted statement distributed so could one copy of this redacted statement be placed before the witness himself? Thank you. Mr. Nikolic, while preparing for your testimony before this Honourable Trial Chamber, we discussed the way in which we could do our best to have your testimony recorded in the transcript in the best possible way. So do remember to pause between question and answer, let us not speak at the same time, let us not overlap. So when a question is put to you, please wait for a few seconds, don't speak too fast, so that the interpreters could interpret this properly, because we want your testimony to be recorded appropriately. Could you please state your full name and surname for the transcript?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: My name is Stevan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nikolic, you have given your statement in Belgrade in February 2003. According to a decision made by the Trial Chamber, certain paragraphs, numbers 30, 32, 39, 40, 41, 42 and 44 have been redacted from your statement, and it was decided that you would testify about those matters, including these paragraphs, before the Honourable Trial Chamber. The remaining part of your statement will be as it is. Mr. Nikolic, you stated that on the 12th of April, 1992, you invited Stevan Todorovic, Mico Ivanovic, nicknamed Mijak, to a meeting, as well as the leaders of this group of the many-coloured ones that appeared in the territory of the village of Batkusa on the 11th of April, 1992, Dragan Djordjevic, nicknamed Crni and Srecko Radovanovic, nicknamed Debeli. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us now, this meeting that you scheduled for the 12th of April, 1992, in Donji Zabar. Was it actually held?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The meeting being was held in Donji Zabar, the way I had scheduled it. Those who I invited to the meeting came to the meeting and in addition to them, Mr. Blagoje Simic attended this meeting as well as Mr. Mirko Jovanovic and there was another group of people and I do not remember exactly what their positions and assignments were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As for the persons present at this meeting, what did you say to them and what did they say to you?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify this. The meeting was scheduled because a group of some 30 men landed in my area of responsibility in the village of Batkusa. In order to establish who these people were and with what kind of assignments they came and who had sent them and on the basis of the orders that I had to receive from my superior command, I scheduled this meeting, the way I did. At this meeting I insisted on this particular information. I wanted to know who these men were. They stated who they were. A group of them stated that they were members of the police of the Republika Srpska Krajina and another group said that they were members of the police of the Army of Republika Srpska. In addition to that, I wanted to say what their tasks were, who invited them and so on and so forth and at this meeting in fact we established that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction not the police of the Army of Republika Srpska but the police of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What have you said? I'm sorry, it's all right. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: At this meeting, we talked about the situation in the area of responsibility of the 17th Tactical Group, and also the reasons why these police forces came. I asked first and foremost for an explanation why they had come because their arrival in my area of responsibility was not announced. It was explained to me that they came in two helicopters, that in the first helicopter were the members of the police of the Serb municipality of Bosanski Samac who were sent for training to Sarengrad near Ilok. And in the second helicopter were the members of the police of the Republika Srpska Krajina. There were about 30 of them. I've already said the group was led by Srecko Radovanovic, nicknamed Debeli, and Dragan Djordjevic, nicknamed Crni.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. At that meeting, did other invited persons take part, and also were there other persons who were simply present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Mr. Stevan Todorovic did most of the talking. He said that he was responsible for the arrival of this group. He contacted them, he organised this, and he took them in and they were supposed to organise -- they were supposed to carry out police work in the territory of Bosanski Samac. In addition to Stevan Todorovic, others also took part in this. Mr. Blagoje Simic said that as far as he knew this was organised by Mr. Todorovic. He thought that it was the right thing to do, that this was proper for Todorovic to organise this and that he didn't want to interfere any more and the others started discussing how they would be engaged, where they would be and so on and so forth. All in all, I could say that the leading person at the meeting was Mr. Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. At this meeting, was it specified under who this group of policemen that had come would be?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: This was specified. Mr. Todorovic said that he took these people in, that he was responsible for their accommodation, for their engagement, and for their work and conduct. I cautioned him saying that these were police forces and that my powers did not include the use of such forces, and he said that it would all be in his hands, including logistic support. He said that he would put up this group in the village of Obudovac near the playing field there and that he would lead them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If I understood you correctly, these people who came were policemen, right, and they were under the responsibility of the police; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. I personally checked the documents of some of them and I saw that they had documents of the police of the Republic of Serb Krajina and of the Serb police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, over here these people were often referred to as volunteers, these people who had come. Can you tell us something about this, whether they could have had the status of volunteers at all in the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, according to the law in the Yugoslav People's Army they could not have become volunteers. I think that Official Gazette I 89 from 1991 is where the Presidency regulated the status of volunteers and how they should be treated. This is the way it was roughly. Volunteers, whoever wanted to enter the police or the military, had to go through the Secretariat for National Defence and until entering the Secretariat for National Defence they are volunteers. The Secretariat for National Defence can do two things. If this volunteer had done his military service on the basis of the level of his training and his military ID, he can be sent to one of the units. If not, then it is the duty of the secretary to send him for an assessment, a psychological and physical assessment and only then can such a person be sent to a unit. When these people get to a certain unit, if they had not gone through their military service, they have to undergo training and only once they have completed their training can they be used in combat operations. Those who had done their military service and had then reached the -- a particular unit have a shorter training and their knowledge is checked and then they start operating within the unit. There is no status of volunteers there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood this correctly, this group that came, according to no regulations that existed then in the Yugoslav People's Army could it have joined the Yugoslav People's Army and obtained the status of a member of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, now we are going to talk about what happened on the 17th of April, 1992. What do you know about the events that occurred between the 16th and 17th of April, 1992? What did you find out? How did you find out about this? Could you please tell the Honourable Trial Chamber about it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Sometime around 3.00 in the morning or perhaps after 3.00 in the morning, I was awakened by the duty officer and he gave me the telephone and it was Mr. Blagoje Simic. He had called me to say the following, roughly: I am calling as president of the Crisis Staff and I wish to inform you that the Serb police and the Serb Territorial Defence have taken measures because there was a danger of a conflict breaking out in Samac. Therefore, they took over Bosanski Samac. They have taken authority in Bosanski Samac. This is under way and it will be finished soon. I cautioned against the possible consequences and I pointed out that what should be avoided at all costs was an interethnic conflict, casualties, and I cautioned him against anything that could be done in this direction. Also I said that my powers do not go that far. I cannot appoint governments and I cannot dismiss governments, but I ask and I insist that this be carried out in a proper way, in order to enable the system to function properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pisarevic, I wonder, Mr. Nikolic, when you say, and this is on page 6, line 25, when you say that Dr. Simic called you and informed you that -- in the English translation it then says the Serb police and the Serb Territorial Defence have taken measures et cetera, can you explain what was meant by Serb Territorial Defence? Just for the sake of clarity, what you understood that to mean.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have understood the question. I must admit that in principle I did not understand what this meant, the Serb Territorial Defence because I had no idea that it had been organised as such. It was quite clear what the Serb police was but I assumed that in the meantime, some units were organised as a Serb Territorial Defence that were placed under the command of the organs of authority, and that they were engaged as such. Later on, in the coming period, it was proven that such units had already been organised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And just one other question. You mention that it was your understanding that these units organised as a Serb Territorial Defence were placed under the command of the organs of authority. Could you perhaps tell us what your meaning is there, the organs of authority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean the Crisis Staff specifically in Bosanski Samac, as the representatives of government, or those who had taken over power in Bosanski Samac at that moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: I have another question. It goes to the transcript, page 6 line 11, the question by counsel, "If I understood this correctly, this group that came, according to no regulations that existed then in the Yugoslav People's Army could have joined the Yugoslav People's Army in the status of a member..." I don't understand that question. I don't think it makes -- I think it makes no sense. Could you perhaps have a look at it and repeat your -- what you intended to ask? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we shall certainly clarify this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have heard what Honourable Judge Lindholm is interested in. The question was the following. This group that came, at that time, could it have directly become part of the Yugoslav People's Army or not? That is the core of this question, if I understood His Honour properly.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a group that belonged to the police forces. There were no grounds whatsoever on which they could become part of the Yugoslav People's Army. The Yugoslav People's Army had combat manpower with certain specialties and it had the military police. That is to say there was no other police. These are professional policemen. I think that you understand what I'm saying. Professional policemen. Police officers that deal with the civilian structure of society.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, let's not go too far. I think that the core of the question put by His Honour is the following: This group or any other group in April, in the month of April, could it have, as such, joined the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It could not have. Only if it were a formation unit that would be sent from some other establishment into the 17th Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, this formation unit would have already been with -- within the JNA and then it would have had nothing to do with volunteers?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this meeting came to an end on the 12th -- oh, yes, yes. So what did you do after that, after Mr. Simic informed you about what had happened?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I called my corps commander, that is my superior commander, commander of the 17th Corps, General Savo Jankovic, and I conveyed to him a preliminary piece of information, what I had learned, that is, and I said that the Serb police and the Serb TO had taken over the key functions in Bosanski Samac. I explained the situation to him in somewhat greater detail, and he said to me that the units of Tactical Group 17 should remain outside what was going on at all costs, outside everything that was going on in Samac. And that we should do our job in accordance with the assignments that the tactical group had been given.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those units of the 17th Tactical Group of the Yugoslav People's Army also included the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's right. The 4th Detachment was part of the tactical group number 17.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment of the JNA, that is what it was called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. You've already explained in your statement what happened next and I will not be asking you about that. But do you remember, and did you discuss with Mr. Simo Zaric the next day, on the 18th of April, 1992, do you remember discussing it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. The next day, but to answer this question with Your Honour's leave I'd need to perhaps explain the situation that the tactical group number 17 was in at the time, namely that is the time when the regular forces of the Republic of Croatia and the forces of the Croat Defence Council had already launched an offensive against the northern part of Posavina. Across the Sava River, across the Bosna [Realtime transcript read in error "boza"] River and from the municipality of Orasje and the village of Domaljevac [Realtime transcript read in error "moemal yea vamp"]?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The major part of the tactical group forces, that is the manoeuvre structures and by this I mean not detachments but units which are mobile which may be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The transcript on page 10, line 19, here it says "boza river" this means Bosna River and the village is Domaljevac on line 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I think that will be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, do go on.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So fighting was already under way at the majority part of the manoeuvreing units of the tactical group number 17 was already being engaged in those combat operations. Under the circumstances, at the time, Mr. Simo Zaric was in Bosanski Samac and in the wake of the events in Bosanski Samac, I told him and Mr. Radovan Antic the commander of the 4th Detachment ordered to first put the detachment on full combat preparedness and in -- early in the morning I issued an additional task to them, telling them that the major part of the detachment should act with the deployment plan, and the deployment plan meant the Defence of the boundary areas of the municipality of Bosanski Samac, that is taking positions on the right bank of the Sava and the right bank of the Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, you already spoke about this in your statement so let us not repeat that all, and my question was: What you're telling us about, it all happened on the 17th, and my question was whether you and how met or talked on the 18th, that is the next day, with Mr. Zaric and what did Mr. Zaric tell you on that occasion? Did he tell you that some members of the 4th Detachment who were of Muslim and Croat ethnicity arrested?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's leading, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. I withdraw this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But tell me, do you remember the 18th of April and so on and so forth, of course what I mean is did you talk with Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the 18th of April, I talked with Mr. Simo Zaric indeed because Mr. Simo Zaric called me from Bosanski Samac and quite upset said, "I'm at the MUP, that is at the police station. There is some problems here because even some members of the 4th Detachment have been arrested, that is members of our regular unit." And he said to me, that he was asking me to take some urgent measures to have those members set free. And I called Mr. Blagoje Simic and he told me when I'm not abreast of what is going on there, this Mr. Todorovic is at the head of these actions so call Mr. Todorovic please and the problem will be solved. I called Mr. Todorovic and after, well, let's say, after pretty heated discussion during which he told me I don't know who members of the 4th Detachment are and I said it's very simple because they all have documents showing that they belong to the 4th Detachment so all you have to do is ask them to show these documents so the understanding was that Mr. Zaric should refer to the authorisation by Mr. Todorovic to take over the members of the 4th Detachment and that is what he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, did Mr. Zaric send you a report telling you that your order had been put through?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did send me a report. We also met, and I was fully briefed about the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Zaric go to the police station and take over the members of the 4th Detachment without your order to that effect?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, if we are talking about the chain of command, two superiors. His first superior was Captain Radovan Antic the commander of the 4th Detachment, and then the next one up the ladder was I. He had nothing to do at the MUP until and unless I ordered him to do something. So he carried out an order that I had given him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, did you speak with Mr. Simo Zaric again and did your command receive information through security agencies? What was going on in Samac and what did Mr. Zaric ask you to do on that occasion when you talked?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: At the time I was busy with combat operations against regular members of the army of the Republic of Croatia and the Croat Defence Council but I was nevertheless also following with attention the developments in Bosanski Samac and not only in Bosanski Samac but throughout the area of responsibility. Mr. Zaric, as the assistant commander of the 4th Detachment for intelligence and security, was duty-bound to monitor the situation in Bosanski Samac. I'm explaining this in order to make you understand the problem. So Mr. Zaric called me and said there are quite a number of arrested members of the Croat and Muslim ethnicity, they are being arrested, some are beaten, they are harassed and one of them had already been killed. That is roughly what Mr. Zaric told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Zaric ask you to protect or in some way try to prevent the arrests of Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. He if I may put it that way, he asked me and requested that I take certain steps to prevent that or to reduce it to the minimum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember what Mr. Zaric asked you to do towards the end of April or rather on the 26th of April, 1992? What did he ask you to do to protect those incarcerated persons?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that. I think it was around the 26th of April, when Mr. Zaric called me. My assistant responsible for security Captain Maksimovic answered the phone and first the two of them talked first and then Makso, that is my security assistant, handed me over the phone and said Mr. Zaric is calling because there is some problems in Samac. Mr. Zaric told me that the treatment of prisoners, that is the detainees, at the police station, and in the TO building, was quite brutal. He said that some had been beaten up and that is when he mentioned that a man had been killed, I believe he said, and said, "Please do something to solve the situation and to rescue those people somehow." And I told him to stay at the police station, that is to stay put, to then contact and call Captain First Class Momcilo Petrovic who was in Brcko to talk to him, to discuss the possibility of transferring those prisoners to Brcko. I said that I'd also call Petrovic and that I would also send Makso Simeunovic, my security assistant to take over those men or to take some steps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Why was it necessary to establish contact with Captain Petrovic and what you said in Brcko? In Brcko what is it a garrison, barracks, where in Brcko to be transferred?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, there was a JNA garrison in Brcko. That garrison had a regular military prison, besides in the barracks there was plenty of room. So that a certain number of detainees could be properly accommodated there and be provided with some decent living conditions. Secondly, pulling them out across the Tinja river, that is outside the area of responsibility of the 17th Tactical Group would practically protect those people because they would be beyond the reach of any other possible reprisals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand your meaning properly, the transfer of prisoners to the garrison in Brcko puts them outside the area of responsibility of the 17th Tactical Group, that is your area of responsibility, and thereby the civilian authorities and -- in Bosanski Samac has no powers over what happens in Brcko; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do? Did you order Makso Simeunovic to carry out that task?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I called my corps commander, General Jankovic explained the situation to him and he said, "Nikolic, you must bear in mind that our competences do not extend that far, that no state of war has been proclaimed." However, I insisted, I wanted to do something for the simple reason, and that was the humanitarian one. We wanted to help those people. And he said, right, do something but please do it elegantly, to avoid any fighting, any bloodshed or anything, because we have no authority to settle accounts with anyone in this manner. After that, I called captain Makso Simeunovic. I ordered him to take sufficient number of vehicles to ensure a police escort [as interpreted], go to Bosanski Samac to establish contact with Mr. Zaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, let us see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours maybe just one word is missing here in the transcript. To ensure military police escort in page 15, line 20. Here it says just police escort and actually he said military police escort.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps the witness can restate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic --

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I ordered my assistant, Makso Simeunovic, the chief of security in the tactical group number 17 to take a certain number of vehicles, sufficient to accommodate all those prisoners, to take -- to get the escort from the military police platoon at the disposal of the tactical group number 17, to go to Bosanski Samac, to meet or rather communicate with Mr. Simo Zaric, and take over the detainees. To my knowledge, Makso Simeunovic carried out this task fully. The -- he transferred the detainees to Brcko. He handed over to the command of the garrison in Brcko, that is the Captain First Class Momcilo Petrovic, handed them over to him, they were accommodated there. He returned, informed me that he had carried out that task, and that was the end of my concern about those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst those people were in the police station in Bosanski Samac and the TO headquarters, did you and your security assistant Mr. Makso Simeunovic, issue any orders to Mr. Simo Zaric regarding the conduct of interviews or rather collection of information about the illegal arming of citizens in the municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Should I explain it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, illegal armament of paramilitary organisations of literally all the parties was under way, we knew that and we were monitoring it. Many of these shipments were seized and measures were instituted against them. There is also some information, that some members of the army, I mean the JNA, also participated in these dishonourable deals, and that is I told Mr. Zaric, as a man who was experienced in police matters, to interrogate a certain number of people whom -- who he -- in his opinion could have some information, to collect this information, and to brief me about this. That is to tell me what it is that he'd learned from them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you enable Mr. Zaric to enter the police station?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I did it by calling Mr. Todorovic. I told him Mr. Zaric is coming, so I urge you to enable him to talk with some of the detainees, because there is reasonable doubt that they have something to do with the weapons contraband, with the cooperation with paramilitary organisations, and there is also doubt that some JNA members are participating in it. Mr. Todorovic said he had nothing against it and Mr. Zaric could do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Mr. Zaric report to you after the task?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, now we shall move on to the event which happened in Crkvina on the 8th of May, 1992. The event in Crkvina is a crime which happened when, in the -- in a -- when 16 people were killed in a warehouse. How did you learn about this event?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel speak into the microphone?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from whom did you learn this?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I learned about this unfortunate incident from Mr. Zaric once again. I suppose in view of the nature of his work and the movement -- area of responsibility of the 4th Detachment and the reconnaissance in the area, that is how Mr. Zaric learned about this event. He called me and said, have you heard about what had happened? He was very upset and I said no, I don't know, what's it about? Since I was busy with combat operations which were already under way. And were very intensive. And he told me that in Crkvina, there had been a crime committed by a man called Lugar, that he had killed 16 people, and that it was -- that it was terrible and that something had to be done about it, that we had to see what we should do. And I listened to him and when he finished I said, "Fine, you do your job and I'll see what is going on and what can be done." I called Mr. Todorovic, and he answered rather diplomatically. He said perhaps it did happen, perhaps it didn't, he doesn't know anything about it but I insisted. I wanted to talk to those who had -- who were involved in this. My signals service has ensured the line to Mr. Radovanovic for me, Srecko Radovanovic called Debeli and the communication with Mr. Djordjevic called Crni. I must admit that they were also pretty upset by this incident and quite taken aback and I asked them what is going on, what has happened? And they thought that Mr. Mirko Lugar, had committed a crime in which he had killed those people while being mentally disturbed, and I said that steps have to be taken to prevent any such thing happening again and so on and so forth and to Todorovic I also said that he should investigate the matter because at that time he represented the police. How far had he gone in his investigation?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, it may assist if we have a date, no date has been given for Mr. Zaric informing Mr. Nikolic of the Crkvina massacre, nor of the witness's conversations with Mr. Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Counsel will deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic I told you that we would be talking about the events of the 8th --

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And the 9th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Tell us when did Mr. Zaric inform you about the crime and when did you talk with Djordjevic and Radovanovic and Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I think it was on the 9th. The 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was early in the morning?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That was in the morning before noon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, did you, after the information that you were given from Mr. Zaric, did you issue any orders to Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I ordered Mr. Zaric, I told him to collect the information, all the information that he could, and to come to me, that is to come to the command post. I also called Makso Simeunovic, chief of security, head, and we -- the three of us sat down and talked a little and I said the following. Knowing that Mr. Zaric knows people of influence in Belgrade, and I also knew a certain number of those people, I said that he should pack his bags, go to Belgrade, communicate with key individuals dealing -- addressing such problems, solving such problems, and jobs of that kind, and to take whatever was necessary to find whatever channels to avoid -- to prevent any such thing happening again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know this individual that Mr. Zaric also knew who worked for the security in the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was his name?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The man that we knew is Colonel Maksimovic, who was born somewhere around Bosanski Samac, I believe that he was born in Obudovac. Mr. Zaric went to see him and through him he talked with the highest security bodies in the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric went to Belgrade and when did he return to Belgrade, did he report to you and what did he tell you, whom did he see and whom did he notify of the crime?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric went to Belgrade, carried out the task, returned, and said that he had informed the security administration of the Yugoslav People's Army practically. At what time it was headed by General Aleksandar Vasiljevic. In addition to Aleksandar Vasiljevic, there were several other people present at the meeting but he was the key person there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you, do you remember that he had also put together an official report of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. He said that at the security administration, an official record had been made of the meeting and that it had been said that this memo would go through all the relevant bodies and that measures would be taken to avoid any such situations happening -- from happening again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you left the area of the municipality of Samac, that is from the position of the commander of 17th Tactical Group, did the 17th Tactical Group cease to exist at the time?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, from the municipality of Bosanski Samac, that is I left the post of the commander of the 17th Tactical Group because it didn't cover all the municipality Bosanski Samac only. I left this position on the 19th of May because I received the -- from the command of the 17th Corps according to which all the members of the Yugoslav People's Army who had not been born in Bosnia-Herzegovina had to return by 2400 hours on the 19th of May and had to report to specified garrisons in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and I did that and I took along all the officers that were there who fell within this category. I turned over the duty and I left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, were you not in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina or Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After that, I was no longer visited that territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honours, I have finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, cross-examination? I see Mr. Pantelic, you want to put some questions? Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct. Cross-examined by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour I do apologise, I have to rearrange my papers. Just a couple of seconds, please. In the meantime, I would also kindly assistance of the -- of Ms. Registrar, if the interpreter's booth can be provided with a copy of P16A ter. It's a transcript, it's a transcript of the video footage that we shall use in these proceedings. Thank you. And also, Mr. Usher, I need your assistance also for interpreter's booth, one copy of the part of Blaskic judgement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Nikolic. My name is Mr. Pantelic and I defend Mr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we begin, would you kindly tell me, the 17th Tactical Group, you were the commander of this group, what was the area of responsibility? Was it north, south, east or west? Please give us the boundaries of the responsibility of the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The zone of responsibility of the 17th Tactical Group was mouth of River Tinja into Sava, so north-east to the east River Tinja to the north River Sava, up until the point where the River Bosna goes into River Sava. The western boundary followed along River Bosna and up until the depth going to Modrica up to the municipality of [Realtime transcript read in error "^"] Gradacac. What's excluded is Orasje and Domaljevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, maybe we need just one small piece of evidence here in the transcript. Until the depth going to Modrica up to the municipality of and here we don't read which one was and it would be helpful now to know which municipality it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before my friends go on, I actually have a large colour map blown up with ten copies which I was going to show to the witness in cross-examination. It may assist Mr. Pantelic if he uses that for the area of responsibility and perhaps the witness marked it on with a text or something at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm grateful to my learned friend, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think the witness can be shown that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I think it will be assistance for all participants. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The writing is not as clear as it could possibly be because it's been blown up from a one to 50.000 but we can certainly work out where everything is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I see that my learned friend has a smaller map. Maybe it will be more convenient for the witness to mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The smaller one is obviously easier to handle. The larger one was because the writing wasn't as distinct but I can certainly give the witness the smaller one if it will assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I have three copies of the smaller one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, you're a retired officer, aren't you? You are a Colonel, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am but I'm retired right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Colonel, kindly take a felt pen, it's a black coloured felt pen?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could the witness have a marker?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, kindly draw a line on this map and show us where the area of responsibility of your tactical group was so that we can clearly understand what is going on. Lots of witnesses have testified on this but you were the commander of this tactical group and we would like to hear this from you. Sir, it doesn't really have to be very precise down to the millimetre. Just so that we can have an idea to the best of your recollection as to what your area of responsibility was. We know that ten years have gone by since. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel, you said that Domaljevac and Orasje were not part of the area of responsibility. Would you kindly show us where that is?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This is Orasje and here we have -- we have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the transcript, I would just like to say that on this map that you drew, the black line drawn by yourself with a felt pen is the area of responsibility of the 17th Tactical Group and the crossed out area is the area that belongs to the municipality of Domaljevac and Orasje and they did not belong to the area of responsibility of the 17th Tactical Group; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have an exhibit number if there is no objection obviously from the other parties?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The map will be treated as Exhibit D180/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 17th Tactical Group, according to military terminology, you know we are laymen here, Colonel, would you kindly explain to us what does the 17th Tactical Group, where does it belong?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It is a temporary formation. The command of the corps, army corps, formed it for the area of which it was supposed to act on and according to the tasks that it has, the formation was temporary and it was only valid for the time, certain time period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regards to the number of soldiers, can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have assistance of my learned friend, in the answer --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the 17th Tactical Group, what is that military unit? What -- how -- what is the level of it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It's at the level of the motorised brigade, for instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many soldiers did you have under your command in the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Depending of the period in question, and the number of people that would answer the call-up, we would have from 3.500, up to 4.700 and up to 4.800 soldiers. Counting the manoeuvrable structures and the non-manoeuvrable structures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So you have explained the structure of the 17th Tactical Group in your statement, under paragraph 19. I will not go over that now. Could you kindly tell me, Colonel Nikolic, you have completed the highest military schools, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As part of your training in those schools, as part of your calling that you obtained, you must have undergone certain regulations and you must know the regulations of the brigade from 1964, this --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 1984. Interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was given by the Secretariat of the national defence, issued by them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The regulations of the -- for the brigade, from 1984, of the Yugoslav People's Army, those regulations talk about the structures of the brigade. Just to remind you, I do have the schematics from that regulation, from that period, and I would like to you give us your comments on it. Colonel Nikolic, we have the schematics here showing us the formation of a brigade. What I'm interested in is the following: Tell us, was this structure also used and applied with regards to the 17th Tactical Group or was it different?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I told you that the rank of the tactical group belongs approximately to the rank of a brigade but the structure was not like this. Before I arrived here, I told Mr. Pisarevic, and I insisted, that I would like to get all the rights to give you the precise information from the Secretariat of National Defence but I did not get this authorisation. However, I will try to answer to the best of my knowledge. All the units are manoeuvre units, meaning that wherever a brigade goes, they go as well. When we talk about a tactical group, a tactical group was composed of a command. It had headquarters and there were also units attached to the headquarters, such as you see here, we have the headquarters and then the reconnaissance unit and the command and that was very similar to the 17th group. We did not have the command for political matters, because we didn't need it and then the security organ was existed at the time because it was linked to the police operations and then we also had the reconnaissance unit. I also said what units the tactical group was composed of but what the particular -- the particularity of this was that it had also non-manoeuvrable structures, meaning that units that are linked to a certain area and everything that took place under the area of responsibility of the 17th Tactical Group, those units never moved from their positions. Those are the detachments of the JNA and the platoons of the JNA, the companies of the JNA, there were four or six, and the number of those units was changing, depending on the situation. The system or the organisation of the command such as we can see it here, of course we did not have the committee of the SKJ and we did not have any political organs if you want, if -- I hope that I've answered clearly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I was just waiting for the end of the translation or the interpretation rather. You have stated that the security organ was subordinate to the units of the superior over the units of the police, as it is described here on the schematics; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is -- that was the case. Makso Simeunovic was my assistant for security and he commanded directly to the units of the military police, which means that I did not have the right to -- it doesn't mean that I didn't have the right to command those units but they were under his command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How many men did that unit of the military police count?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: About 30 members. It was -- it had the strength of a platoon, and three men from that unit were in charge of my personal security, whereas the other departments were in charge of all other police tasks. One department was carrying out all the police tasks and the other one was taking care of the -- regulating the traffic. The three men who were part of my personal security team, I can tell you that one was Edin, he was a Muslim; another one was Pero, he was a Serb; and the third one was Cule [phoen], he was a Croat. I just want you to know that...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 115, at paragraph 115 of this regulation, we talk about the role of the commander of the brigade and I would like to read it out for you, just to remind you, although I'm sure you know it by heart.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have no problem about showing certain documents and certain sketches to the witness but we have not received these documents earlier, and what is Mr. Pantelic wants to quote to the witness we don't know that so if he does want to do that, could it be pleased be placed on the ELMO so that we know what he's talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, no problem. It's actually a part of the regulation that already Colonel Nikolic said that he's familiar with during his education and I'm simply would like to refresh his memory. It's no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, the Trial Chamber is of the view that you should concentrate on the areas which was touching your client which the witness discussed in his evidence. We don't need all these details at all, all these matters that you're discussing. Go to the events that happened on the dates that the witness has discussed in relation to the activities of your client, attendance of the meeting, the telephone call, and matters such as were mentioned by this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is why your cross-examination is limited to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will do that, Your Honour, no problem with me. I just want a very briefly cover the issue of the role of Colonel Nikolic in that regard because directly and indirectly it's relevant to the case of my client. So I will be very concise and very efficient, if you allow me. I will not go into details, no, Your Honour. I will do --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because he has already explained what his role was. We don't need a repetition of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nikolic, as part of your training, and background, I imagine that you were acquainted with the regulation issued by the Presidency of SFRJ in 1988 with regards to what to do in case of war?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour it's just a part of this important document which I already tendered into evidence, just to have a confirmation of his personal knowledge of the role of commander with regard to the international humanitarian law and conventions. It's just one paragraph, Your Honour, related to the events in Samac. If you allow me, please. It's just a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution knows where Mr. Pantelic is going on this. We certainly don't object to him pursuing this. I mean subject to Your Honour's directions of course pursuing this for a limited period, this small area in which he wishes to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, Your Honour, the regulations that Mr. Pantelic is evoking, it is the way the international humanitarian law is seen in case of war, and if I recall correctly, the Colonel said that the state of war was never proclaimed. I just wanted to explain what my learned colleague is probably trying to do and we are not objecting to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I think it's a matter for the final judgement of this Trial Chamber, whether it was conflict or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, you can go over what you wanted to cover but very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very briefly, yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, tell us are you aware of this regulation on how to apply the international humanitarian law, this regulation from 1988 so how to apply the humanitarian law in case of war, this regulation replaced the one from 1972. Are you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I did not understand your -- I didn't hear actually your interpretation because I just heard the interpreter's all of a sudden say something but I didn't follow your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Terribly sorry. Tell us, are you familiar with the regulation on how to apply the international humanitarian law in case there is a war in the former Yugoslavia in the regulation of 1988 which replaced the regulation issued in 1972?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: All the commanders of the former JNA are familiar with those regulations, and that particular regulation was applied throughout all the units. That was the principle of our work. Every time when there was a new regulation, the new order, it was always applied and it was published in the Official Gazette, all members had to get familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will agree with me undoubtedly that as part of those regulations and orders, we can see that there is a definition about the personal responsibility in case of a violation of law of war. What was your answer to this question?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I said yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These regulations also talk about the responsibility of military commanders and they state their responsibility with regards to the doings of their subordinates; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These regulations also make sure that the -- or talk about the violations of the laws of war?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I cannot remember textually the way it is written.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Obviously our friends from interpretation booth are not in good shape and form this morning so we have to repeat again. The transcript is not accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question is the following: Or was the following: Amongst other things, these regulations talk about the procedure on how to find and how to make sure that the evidence is collected when there is a violation of the laws of war?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I do not remember them textually. I couldn't recite them to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, of course. We did not want to go into details here. We just wanted to make sure that you're aware of these facts. My colleague, Mr. Pisarevic, asked you a question about your understanding of volunteer units and your understanding of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit D166/1, please? Your Honour, I believe it's time for our break. Maybe we can leave this topic until after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, we still have a minute to go. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. From this angle, I cannot see the official watch and that's why --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nikolic --

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to you look at this regulation -- order. You were in the 17th Tactical Group, but tell us, when did you become a member of it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It was in the end of the month of October, 1991. It's when the creation started of the 17th Tactical Group and I ended the creation of this group on the 15th of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This order is from the month of December of 1991. I would like you to look at point 7?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Because this is not any order. This is something different that we have here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's my mistake, sorry, Your Honour. I do apologise. Although we should discuss that document too but Your Honour now I believe it's 10.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We shall take our break and continue at 1100 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Could we have Exhibit D177/1, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it's easier, because the print is very small, you can take it and you can read it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that they do not have a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since this is an order of the Presidency of Yugoslavia, were you aware of it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In item 7, it says that within ten days, all individuals and forces that are outside the armed forces of the SFRY should accord their positions and all individuals and groups of volunteers will be removed, all of those who do not carry this out. Did you have any such cases in the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We had a case in the 17th Tactical Group when a group of volunteers came who were somewhere on the front line, and I think there were about 15 of them. As for these 15 odd men, I personally, since they did not have any documents, no proof whatsoever of having been sent by an appropriate authority, I had them disarmed, I put them into vehicles at the Sava River near Raca, I transferred them back and practically expelled them from my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic, do you think that we could just clarify in the translation here, page 33, line 13, where your question, it comes as a question, two questions in a row, I think, in any way, in any event, it says, the armed forces of the SFRY should accord -- accord, their positions. I am just wondering what that means, accord their positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Should -- it's issue of translation. Authorised is better translation, instead of accord, should authorise their presence within the zone of responsibility of a particular JNA units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since the persons you mentioned arrived by helicopter -- I shall repeat this, since the persons you mentioned arrived by military helicopter, I'm referring to the people were Serbia who introduced themselves as representatives of the police of Krajina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when speaking to them, did you find out how come they reported to these units and arrived by military helicopter in Batkusa? Did you find out how they were engaged?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, they came at the request of Mr. Stevan Todorovic, who had some connections in Belgrade and they came to work on police activities in the territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac. All of them had IDs and I claim with full responsibility because I saw them that they had IDs of the MUP of the Republika Srpska Krajina or IDs of the MUP of the Republika Srpska. I informed my corps commander about that, after the meeting, and after these facts were established and then he said to me that allegedly, I mean I don't know whether it's this way, there is an agreement between Republika Srpska and the Republic of Srpska Krajina on mutual assistance and cooperation. And this was purportedly the reason why they came, the fact that they arrived in helicopters of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, in agreement with the higher command, what did you do about putting them under control of your tactical group or rather under your personal command?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is a double-barrelled question. I have no problem for witness to answer this question but this question cannot be simply answered. First he's putting them under control of your tactical group or your personal command. These are two very, very different things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, can you rephrase your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, you informed your superior command the 17th Corps, about their arrival?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I did not hear the question because of this other thing I was hearing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You informed your superior command, the 17th Corps, about their presence in your area of responsibility; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what were the instructions of the 17th Corps regarding their stay in your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I explained a while ago that the commander of the corps said to me, since these are members of the police, we do not have any authority over them and that I have no authority to put them under my command unless I submit a special request and then this request would be granted at a certain level, then this kind of order would come to the head of MUP and to me, and then they could be engaged somewhere. On the other hand, they were not under my control. Am I clear?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your stay until the 19th of May, 1992, did you use the members of these alleged units of the Krajina police in some combat operations?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I used members of the Serb police, or rather members of the police of the Serb municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo under formation. That would be a precise answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use Lugar and Crni in military operations?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I used all that I got from MUP, from Mr. Todorovic, and in accordance with my own requests. My request went to the corps commander or rather the commander of the 17th Corps. He had his own lines and connections through which this went, and then Mr. Todorovic and I both received orders accordingly. I that I could and he that he could place at my disposal the forces I needed. Had a state of war been proclaimed, then in fact everybody would have been under my command. Then that would have meant the organs of authority, the organs of the police, and the business community, the economic sector. When there is a state of war, then they are all under the command of the army but that was not the case then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, Lugar, Crni and Debeli were used in military operations under your command?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Between 40 and 50 members of the Serb police of the Serb municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo were used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Colonel Nikolic, which officers of the command of the JNA air force did you know in Belgrade? Who did you maintain contact with?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I did not know -- well, I knew in principle who the commanders of the air force corps were, et cetera but I did not have anyone special. The only person I spoke to once was Colonel Jeremic. This was some kind of air support, as to whether it would be there or would not be there and his telephone was the contact telephone so no one personally. I mean even Mr. Jeremic, I didn't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because Simo Zaric, in his book, on page 259, says that when you send him to Belgrade, to visit, if necessary, some of his people and your people in the command of the air force, so I'm interested in hearing who this pertains to. Is this Colonel Jeremic or some other person?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. Wait a minute. The command of the air force could not have influenced the situation in Tactical Group 17 or in the 17th Tactical Corps at all unless it is air support or something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could we have the English page number? There was the B/C/S page number of 259. Could we have the English page number if possible, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately I don't have the English version with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I may have the floor for one second? Your Honours we still don't have a ruling of the Trial Chamber in respect to Mr. Zaric's book so at this point I'm a bit curious about the situation what is going to be, because Mr. Pantelic obviously is using and quoting portions of the book as they are so...

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I note that Mr. Lazarevic did exactly the same thing with Mr. Simeunovic's evidence. I don't have the transcript page reference with me at the moment. I have it upstairs but I certainly found that in re-examination of Mr. Simeunovic after Mr. Pantelic's cross-examination, Mr. Lazarevic himself quoted passages or extracts from Mr. Zaric's book in relation to the Brcko incident so the Defence itself has already put the book into -- put sections of the book into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can confirm what my learned colleague said it was during re-examination because of some misquoting but the issue of the use of Mr. Zaric's book during proceedings was raised later and we are awaiting for a ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The ruling which the Trial Chamber has yet to deliver is whether or not the whole book should be produced in evidence. But as far as the excerpts that parties are using, which are relevant to the issues that are under discussion, that can be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel Nikolic, he mentions some of his people and your people at the command of the air force. Let's be very precise. Who were your people at the command of the air force?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I did not have my people in the air force. If you mean by that some special connections or friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it is an uncontested fact that Lugar and his group came by helicopters of the air force; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: According to eyewitness statements, that's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Nikolic, the period I'm interested in is October 1991 until your departure from the area of Samac Posavina, that is the 19th of May. Tell me, in that period, did you as commander of the 17th Tactical Group make plans with the leadership of the SDS in Samac about military operations, including the takeover of authority by armed force in Samac? Could you describe this to the Trial Chamber what your relations with the SDS were?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: My relations with any members of any party was -- were non-existent so in fact I didn't have anything with the SDS or the SDA or the HDZ. If there were any relations, these were relations where I could and always did receive people. I talked to people regardless of the party they belonged to. All of this with the objective of bringing the situation back to normal, if possible, and also keeping law and order. I did not take part in any plans that were being elaborated by the SDS if so, or I was not a member of any party. I'm not a member of any party nowadays either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we will agree that the SDS and specifically Blagoje Simic did not make any plans with you as commander of the 17th Tactical Group on joint activity and forcible takeover of power in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's right. I often talked to Mr. Simic and Mr. Todorovic but these were conversations that had nothing to do with military actions. They were interested, like anybody else, in what was going on, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any rate, on the basis of intelligence information that came to the 17th Tactical Group you personally had knowledge that a programme of illegal arming was taking place within the area of responsibility of the 17th Tactical Group, by the SDA and the HDZ; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I did have knowledge that there was an illegal arming of all parties, the SDA, the SDS and the HDZ, precisely due to such information I insisted that Mr. Zaric talk to all the persons who were detained. We received information through our intelligence service, I got it also through my scouts, and also through radio reconnaissance. I must say that processing this information at the level of the tactical group and the 17th Corps was correct, and that we did have a picture of what was taking place, who was being armed, and to what extent this had gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have now Exhibit D166/1, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Take a look at this document. You can take it into your hands so you can see it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the interpreters please have a copy on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at these two pages?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is it possible to have a copy on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please put your copy on the ELMO so that we could follow it as well? Tell me, Colonel, just put it on -- where you had put it. Yes. Now, tell me, did you personally ever see this document?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain when, on which occasion and in which period?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You see, I think that this document encompasses the month of March, the end of March, rather, and the beginning of April. This is a document that we discussed in the command of the 17th Corps at a particular briefing. The document that was compiled by our military intelligence service on the basis of collected data on the situation in terms of who was armed and where in various areas, within the area of responsibility of the 17th Corps. This is a document that was sent to the security organs and we were all familiarised with it. It was updated and corrected on the basis of new information received. We sent new information to the 17th Corps, the command of the 17th Corps to us, and then we corrected what had changed or improved in a particular area or unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically, I'm interested in the following: On the basis of your intelligence information from your zone of responsibility and in relation to this document, does this mean that the SDS in your area of responsibility did not have any armed formations?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The document shows that it didn't, and it is true that it is --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not talking about other municipalities.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We are not talking about other municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at page 2. Can you remember, since more than ten years have elapsed, in your area of responsibility, what were the villages here where there were forces of the HDZ, as it is mentioned here, what was the information that you got from the field, the intelligence information you got in the period from October 1991 until April, mid-April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I have understood your question. You see, a short while ago, when I marked the area of responsibility, you saw that I excluded Orasje and Domaljevac. That was not accidental. That was because this was an area that was populated by Croats almost 100 per cent, and my commander said that there is no reason for us to touch this, for a simple reason so that people would not be upset in any way, et cetera. However, they were used as a basis for having the regular forces of the Republic of Croatia come to the territory of Bosnia and as a basis for setting up Croat Defence Council units. So critical places were Orasje, Domaljevac, I think -- I can't say exactly now, I can't just say it off the cuff, Hasici, et cetera. These were these areas that were grouped over there where that bend of the Sava River is, where the Tinja flows into the Sava. We even knew that they had anti-aircraft guns and during a particular reconnaissance of mine, the helicopter that I was in, was hit by an anti-aircraft gun from one of those villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that there was rather intensive activity from the autumn of 1991 until April, 1992, by Croat units in terms of preparing for an attack on Posavina?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We can agree in principle. However, from the month of March, perhaps the beginning of April, all of this was intensified, and serious forces were there. We know that the 101st Brigade of the ZNG was engaged there and the 108th Brigade and the 106th Brigade of the HVO, if you allow me I have to say one more thing. Why I know this. I know this for a simple reason, because we took prisoners, some of the members of these units. Perry Colton, an American, is a person who we took prisoner because he destroyed the bridge on the Tinja river. When we took him prisoner, he said publicly on television that he belongs to the reconnaissance and scouting unit of the 101st Brigade of the ZNG. And I also have to say that 17th Tactical Group also had a radio reconnaissance unit, platoon that was put at its disposal. So we listened to entire conversations so I don't think that there could have been any serious surprises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did Simo Zaric inform you as to whether he perhaps talked to members of the SDS about armament? Did you get any kind of information from Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I did not have such information. You see, in Bosanski Samac, we established the 4th Detachment of the JNA. On a few occasions, at the memorial centre, I held meetings with reserve officers, irrespective of their ethnicity and I was convincing people that the only possible solution for keeping the situation as it was from preventing a conflict was that everybody should join this detachment or such detachment. That was the solution. So at that moment, in that place, there was not a special reason for doing anything on the sly over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Simo Zaric in his book on page 168 says that there was a meeting between the HDZ and the SDA on the 19th of March in Prud and he speaks about the well organised operative work of the army and also a man that was planted there at that meeting. What do you know about that particular event?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I know that this meeting was held. I know that we had an intelligence man of ours there and I cannot give you that person's name. At any rate we did have full information. We knew literally quite everything that would happen and we knew what they were planning and we knew who attended the meeting and we could make some estimates in terms of what would happen in the future.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 169, Simo Zaric, then says that in the command of the 17th TG, one expected a strike of the Muslim-Croat police on Samac. Does this confirm what you just said?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does. Two things have to be distinguished here. One thing is what the civilian authorities in Samac did, and the -- it is another matter what the Tactical Group 17 did. Tactical Group 17 and I'd like to be given a minute to explain certain things. It had three principal tasks. The first one was to prevent the transfer of the combat operations from Republic of Croatia to the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, so this was the first task; the second task was preventing the outbreak of a major interethnic conflict; and the third task was to control and secure the communications in the area of responsibility in order to ensure an unhampered supply of the JNA units and the population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
