utterances.text: I have to interrupt you because you've already said that in your statement so let us please be efficient. When we talked before your testimony about the information that you had, you mentioned that sometime around the 10th or 11th April, 1992, so-called tongue was caught and from that man, you learned a number of things concerning the technical [as interpreted] group 17. So could you tell us who was this tongue whom you captured?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Why, yes. He was a member of regular Croat -- Croatian Army units who was caught by our reconnaissance patrols and after the interrogation, he gave us a certain number of information. He was then transferred to the prison in Sremska Mitrovica and from there, he was exchanged within the framework of the exchanges which were taking place like everybody else. At that time, we learned more or less that across the River Sava, across the Bosna River, and from the area of Orasje, Domaljevac, there could be an attack between the 12th and the 17th of April. Now, the date was the problem. That was what that prisoner stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you are coming close to one hour for your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this particular part is relevant to the forcible takeover subcharge 1 in the indictment, all these events. We heard a lot of testimonies from Prosecutor's witnesses regarding the pre-conflict period in Samac, saying that they didn't -- they were not involved in any kind of preparation, there was no military movements, et cetera. The position of the Defence is the following: The absolutely legitimate action to prevent the incursion from Croatian side was of JNA, 4th Detachment and all forces there, specifically 17th Tactical Group, due to the fact that they were in possession of the possible attack from Croatia and they reacted. It's absolutely in accordance with the military doctrine. The Prosecution has the opposite approach and the Trial Chamber will make the final judgement. So it is of the relevance for the Defence case to elicit and to have from such important witness, a military person, number 1, in this region. So we have to conclude, to finalise, all previous evidences heard here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And one, if I may, one small correction for the transcript, on page 44, line 23, concerning the here it says technical 17, this means 17th Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic, I'm just wondering, I mean in terms of the relevance to the indictment and the Defence of your client, Dr. Simic, the emphasis surely is on the night of the takeover, or the early morning of the takeover. Why the 17th Tactical Group and the 4th Detachment did nothing to stop the takeover, and the connection between the 17th Tactical Group, the 4th Detachment and the civilian authorities headed by your client, Dr. Simic. I mean I think those are things that we need to have information on, and maybe not necessarily all of the details about the radio reconnaissance and so on. I mean I think we have enough of that now to show that this was being done and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will establish the evidences with that regard. First of all, we think that -- my client was not a part of any forcible takeover. Secondly, our position is that the military operation was absolutely legitimate in order to prevent the incursion from the Croatian side, and in the fact -- in light of the fact that Serbia Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was established in January and after that, Serbian municipality Samac and Pelagicevo in formation, we have this position, that everything was legitimate. Specifically with regard to the military operation, the position of Defence of Dr. Blagoje Simic is that he personally, nor he, nor the other civilian authorities, were not involved in this kind of military action, kind of prevent action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely the point, that you go to the crucial role which the Crisis Staff played, because it's in that capacity that your client is involved in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct, and I tried to find this relation with the military organs, with the military authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ergo, let's conclude, Colonel Nikolic, can we agree that on the basis of the previous intelligence available to the 17th Tactical Group, and in line with the military doctrine, everything was done to forestall any attack of the Croatian forces from Prud and that side?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The units of the Tactical Group 17 did everything they could to prevent the incursion of the regular Croatian forces into the territory of Bosnia or members of the Croat Defence Council who already were in the territory of Bosnia and to prevent their incursion in the area of responsibility of the tactical group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the 16th and 17th April, 1992, Mr. Simo Zaric on page 212, referring to the period of the time when the operation of the seizure of weapons from armed civilians, that is unlawful armaments in Samac started. He said then that it was necessary to cooperate with the police and the volunteers in the defence of the town and it was coordinated through the command of the 17th Tactical Group. Do you agree with Simo Zaric's view?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I do not agree with that position. I've told you what was the task of the 4th Detachment. The majority of forces of the 4th Detachment took the right bank of the Sava and the right bank of the Bosna, to prevent the Croatian forces forcing their crossing into Bosnia. A platoon, a reinforced platoon, was designated to collect weapons, but I ordered literally to Simo Zaric and Antic and I mean the commander of the detachment, these may not be breakings into houses, these may not be seizure by force. It needs to be done in a civilised -- in an urban manner and why was that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Because that day around 12.00 somebody called Ibela, whatever his name was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, sorry. I have to interrupt you because we are going into this unnecessarily?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: So my answer is no there was no such coordination. The detachment did its part of the job and the police did its part of the job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, before you proceed, can the witness complete his answer because he was stopped by you when he was trying to say because somebody called Ibela. Can the witness complete his answer, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you please, you mentioned Ibela?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Well, the thing is that a Muslim called Ibela called me and he must have seen me somewhere meanwhile during my stay there, so he called me and said openly, "I command a group of an illegal Muslim unit that has been armed by the SDA. What should I do?" And I told him, "Don't do anything, just go home and the members of the 4th Detachment turn up, when they fetch up in front of your house then bring out the weapons that you don't have licences for and hand them over." And that is how it was done. That is what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Simo Zaric several times spoke to the OTP and I'm referring to the one of the 3rd of June, 1998, and this is P142 exhibit. And when Simo Zaric on page 22 spoke about the takeover of Samac, he, in answer to the investigator's question, said the following: "I think that part of the responsibility should be borne by the command of the 17th Tactical Group and I mean Mr. Nikolic." Do you have any reason to doubt the veracity of Mr. Zaric's words, his answer to the Prosecutor, just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, my responsibilities is mentioned here and I cannot answer yes or no. We have to clear up these matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, I'm asking you about this part?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honours we are sorry but everybody is speaking over each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe the witness could be shown page 22 of the interview and then give his command. I have it right here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The usher can take that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No problem, P142, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And Mr. Pantelic, please avoid speaking over the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see down at the bottom, I said not going into your interpretation because you will explain it to counsel Pisarevic when he asks you about this and I'm asking you very concretely, do you have any reason to doubt the veracity of Simo Zaric, who told the Prosecutor's Office that he believed that part of the responsibility should be borne by the command of the 17th Tactical Group and he's referring to Mr. Nikolic. Do you have any doubts about that or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The way it was said, said maybe, it is some opinion or something, and Mr. Pantelic is trying to ask the witness whether he has reason to doubt about facts. These are not facts that was stated in this statement, these are some possible conclusions, some understanding or something like that but not facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's a position of Simo Zaric, according to his personal knowledge. I want to see from this witness, Your Honour, whether he shared that knowledge or whether he has some sort source of his personal knowledge or opinion, simply as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What Mr. Lazarevic is saying is that you should have put it precisely as it was said by Mr. Simo Zaric, that it was his conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's a conclusion of Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any way, the witness has got the text and he has read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He can give his comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, he can comment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell us, what do you think about this?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I've read the text. It is vague. One cannot see what kind of responsibility is meant when the command of the 17th Tactical Group is mentioned. Of course, I've made mistakes in my life and I'm sure that the command of the 17th Tactical Group also had its shortcomings but I really do not see in this text what is it that Simo thinks. What is it that he blames us for specifically. That is what I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, Colonel. Simo doesn't say that. Nobody is guilty but do you agree with me when I say that the 17th Tactical Group headed by you personally did everything within its power to prevent the attack of the Croatian troops on Samac, including the takeover of the vital positions in the town of Samac? Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The counsel is again speaking over the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's absolutely another topic Your Honour, I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: He's talking about the takeover of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's another topic Your Honour, I don't understand the intervention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have one person speaking at a given time? Mr. Lazarevic, what is your intervention?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My invention was that what this portion of Mr. Zaric's interview indicating -- it has nothing to do with the question of Mr. Pantelic. He was referring about the takeover of Bosanski Samac, and asking two questions, first whether the 17th Tactical Group has any role in the takeover. The other one was whether they have done anything in what respect, to do the takeover, to avoid the takeover, to do something against the takeover? I really didn't understand what it has to do with this portion of the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I said, I finished with this interview. That's another line of questioning. It's not -- there is nothing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: As far as you're concerned, the witness gave the answers to your questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm going to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I answer this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll have to repeat the question for the transcript. Do you agree with me when I say that the 17th Tactical Group under your command did its utmost to prevent the incursion in Samac of the Croatian troops, including a preemptive action of taking over the vital positions in the town of Samac on the 16th, 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I agree with the first part of your question. The Tactical Group 17 did all within its power, in its area of responsibility, to prevent the incursion of Croatian forces. We did not take Bosanski Samac. Of the vital facilities in Bosanski Samac, I only put some observers on the silos and those who were checking fire and I believe I'm clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that is what I want to know. I'm talking about the 17th -- 16th and 17th of April. Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, no, no please, we are talking as of the moment when I raised the combat preparedness to a higher level so that is the time I'm talking about. When I raised the combat preparedness and it started at about 11.00 in the morning on the 17th but before that, we had not taken any positions in Bosanski Samac, nor had we had any part in the takeover of power in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put it to you, if I suggest to you, that members of some detachments of the 17th Tactical Group participated in the preemptive takeover of vital facilities in Samac between the 16th and 17th of April, 1992, will you then agree with me?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That is possible, but I did not authorise that. I am not aware of such a case. I am aware of some cases when, for instance, people who were engaged in the first JNA detachment were at the same time were at the disposal of the TO. I know of such a case. And when I tried to investigate why was that first preliminary report, why did it say the police and the Serb TO, and I inferred that somebody from there had been engaged and sent somewhere as TO, and then it did transpire so later on, because the commander of the 1st Detachment, Mico Ivanovic [Realtime transcript read in error "me yat"], Mijak, was subsequently appointed the commander of the TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the security assistant was?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Stevan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean in the 1st Detachment?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's right, Stevan Todorovic was the security assistant and that is why we seriously investigated the detachment later on to see what had happened there. It is quite possible that somebody acted against the orders and they forgot involved somewhere but that was without our knowledge. I hope I was quite clear now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, the complete answer, last answer starts at page 53, line 22, until page 54, line 2. Just for the record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But of course we shall agree that the 1st Detachment was part of the 17th Tactical Group, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we shall also agree that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, we have a problem, maybe counsel and witness are speaking too fast but obviously here we have a 1st Detachment on page 54, line 9, and then there is here on page 53, line 19, Mico, here it says something "me yat", actually it's Ivanovic, Mico Ivanovic, nicknamed Mijak.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let's clear this up. The 1st Detachment was an integral part of the 17th Tactical Group, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as the commander of the 17th Tactical Group, did you on the 17th of April, 1992, take certain measures against the - how shall I put it - unauthorised military involvement of some of the members who were under your command? What did you, for instance, do with regard to the commander of the 1st Detachment and his security assistant?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Let me say, Stevan Todorovic quit the detachment and came to be the Chief of Police or whatever you call it. And Mico Ivanovic stayed on. We had no proof that he had misused his position, although even before that, an interview was conducted with him in which he had to explain what he had been doing at the time when those two helicopters landed. And his explanation was then, since it was his area of responsibility, that was why he had gone out and met those helicopters -- and saw those helicopters land. Then when I had already left, it turned out that they were playing a twofold game and they were showing a collusion between Todorovic, Ivanovic and Milos Bogdanovic. So to make it clearer to the -- Your Honours, the collusion between Todorovic, commander of the 1st Detachment, Mico Ivanovic, and the late Milos Bogdanovic who was killed and he was the head of the Secretariat for National Defence and he was the one who issued summonses, who called up people and sent them to combat units. But it also happened that there, in the 1st Detachment, they had dual -- dual combat orders, combat assignments but that transpired on later, and after I'd left, and I have no reason to talk about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you start any proceedings before the military court against Stevan Todorovic, who had left the unit unauthorised?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It wasn't unauthorised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was it with your accord?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Milos Bogdanovic appointed another man and Todorovic was removed from that position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But you must know that towards the end of April, 1992, Simo Zaric was appointed the head of national security in the territory of the municipality of Samac whilst at the same time he was still an officer?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't understand, what does it mean head for national security?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any information that in late April, 1992, Simo Zaric was appointed head for national security in the municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, I do not have such knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, your relations with -- your relationship with Simo Zaric is a special one. Explain to the Chamber why did you send Simo Zaric to Belgrade to report about the incident in Crkvina rather than your security assistant, Makso Simeunovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We already have the answer, the witness was talking in pretty much details about all this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the chain of command in the army, your assistant was Makso Simeunovic, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wasn't he the one who should have taken certain measures at the higher body?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, measures can be taken by the one whom I order it to, and who I should order it to is up to me because I'm the commander and I decided that it should be Mr. Zaric because he knew people. Had I sent Mr. Makso Simeunovic, he would have probably wander around Belgrade looking for who to talk to and it's a question whether somebody would agree to receive him. So there was a problem there. And therefore, I sent Mr. Simo Zaric, and when I -- when you said that my relationship with Simo Zaric was a special one, I must respond to it in this way. When I was appointed the commander of 17th Tactical Group and when I was sent to form it, I didn't -- I didn't fall out of the blue into this area, because I had come already in possession of certain information. I did not meet Mr. Simo Zaric by accident. I already had information that Mr. Zaric had rescued JNA soldiers who were fleeing from the fire opened on them by Croatian units and getting them out, rescuing them from the Sava River. Mr. Simo Zaric was doing, you know, whenever you go somewhere, you go with some information, you go there with reason, and you therefore establish contact with people who prove to be reliable, who prove to be humane and so on and so forth, even acquaintanceships we didn't just come across one another in the street and by happen stance I came to know Mr. Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you should be winding up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nikolic, I must ask you to cut your answers shorter to try to answer yes or no and so on and so forth and then you will explain it to Mr. Pisarevic because you are wasting time?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I shall happy to do it but please ask me questions so that I can answer them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any rate, there is a question that they are leading questions --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The counsel and witness are not breaking between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, you should know better about pausing and you should be winding up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simo Zaric in his conversations with the Prosecution, on page 142 of the document, speaks of the moment when he started -- when he got his retirement on the 1st of September, he said he was then mobilised by the JNA and he was with General Jankovic in Tuzla, he had a meeting with him, and he was also -- another person was also there, Mr. Masulovic, who was the assistant of the general and you were also present during this meeting. During that meeting, did you engage Simo Zaric practically as your man who would be responsible for the tactical group, for this area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In general terms, yes, if you will, but I would like to explain. In order to appoint somebody at the position of an information officer or a security officer, one must check everything and one must also give his agreement with the previous -- we were the -- with the superior officer so this person can be work -- rather in this position. You cannot proceed without any verifications.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand you fully. Tell me now, since the 5th Detachment of the 17th Tactical Group was located in Obud -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Obudovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you tell us when this unit in charge of the manoeuvre tasks was created, this unit that had a name, this special name tactical group, can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It is not a unit that comes from a 5th Detachment headed by Captain Zoranovic. It is a company belonging to the 1st Motorised Battalion. It is a manoeuvre unit, and we took one of these companies and we trained this company and that company was my reserve company. The reserve company of the commander of the 17th Tactical Group for intervention, when the moment was appropriate, whenever there was a problem and when the problem would become so great they would have to intervene.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of this special unit?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The commander of this special unit was Captain Grbic. I cannot recall his first name at this present time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, your time is over now. You have decided to use --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just need ten minutes to finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. We gave you enough time. We directed you as to which areas you should be concerned with, about the Defence of your client, and you've decided to use your time according to your best solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, please, I just have five positions of my client and I'm done, please, with regard to that. It's only a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours the Prosecution doesn't object to Mr. Pantelic -- we understand there might have been a little time wasted but if there are matters which he feels are necessary to the Defence of his client but has not yet put, perhaps he could outline those so the Trial Chamber knows and could control it that way. Because we don't want to stop him putting all matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Re, the point is he was directed by the Trial Chamber as to which areas he should be concerned with but he decided to use and he has used up so much time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But if he hadn't put those matters to the witness which are vital to his Defence for whatever reason there could be problems later if he doesn't do so now. And if it's only going to take a little bit more time in the context of the entire trial it may not be time wasted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, we shall give you ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My client has these following positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Before that, Your Honour, please, I would like to introduce one document into evidence. Mr. Usher, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is it a new document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's a Prosecution document. It was disclosed to the Defence a long time ago. Three copies for the Bench, two, and one for the Defence, please -- for the Prosecution, please. It's ERN number 0063-6936.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, Mr. Nikolic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is the description of the document? What is the title?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's a note with a telephone number and the name of the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nikolic, you told me that after the 19th of May, you were transferred to Cuprija and you became a commander of the unit of the JNA; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. Just tell us yes or no?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you consult this document, tell us, please, is this the telephone number of your garrison in Cuprija. If you remember?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, I do not remember. My telephone was 053.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the telephone number?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It was a number from Jagodina and not a number from Cuprija. It is quite possible that this is the central, main number of the switch board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't catch the number the witness was giving earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go, let's take it one number at a time, please. This is a switch board number in Jagodina?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It's possibly a number of the military switch board in Cuprija -- Jagodina, sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your nickname is Kriger, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: My nickname is Lieutenant Colonel Kriger. It has been Kriger ever since I was a lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The witness didn't repeat his telephone number. There was an intervention by the interpreters. In order to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, Your Honour, I switch on that because he said that's a probably -- it's line 17, page 61, it's probably a number of the military switch board in Cuprija, the unit that he was deployed so I don't need any particular -- his personal numbers et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it was said what his number was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes and it should be -- it should be recorded because the interpreters didn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your private number at the time, sir?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I said to the Trial Chamber the following: I wanted to say what was the number that was entered under my name as a commander and it is 222430. I remember it very clearly now. 222430. That was the number, with the area code 035. That is the Jagodina area code but it was transferred to that number, it was direct line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the number that figures on this note is the number of the switch board of the military unit in Cuprija; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is quite possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your nickname Kriger comes from an officer, it was a series in the former Yugoslavia, and that was the name of the role of an actor?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, Stevo Zigon was playing that role and I was wearing glasses and I looked like him and that's why I was nicknamed Kriger because in that television series his name was Kriger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a SS officer, isn't he, or the Wehrmacht?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is how you're using your time, you see? This is a problem with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, if I put to you that Lugar Miljkovic was with you, was in touch with you, in contact with you, before and after you were hired in Samac, would you -- would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put to you that you were responsible for the area of responsibility or in the area of responsibility for all the volunteers, including killings, beatings, mistreating people, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put to you that on the 16th, the night between the 16th to the 17th of April, 1992, there was no Serb Crisis Staff in existence, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The gentleman said that Blagoje Simic was the President of the Crisis Staff, whether it existed, when it was formed, I don't know, but I all know that everybody was making Crisis Staff, the HDZ, SDS, SDA, everybody was forming Crisis Staffs so I don't know when this one was formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put to you that Blagoje Simic never called you at 3.00 a.m. on the 17th of April in Pelagicevo, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. I will not agree with you because I did receive that phone call.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put to you that you, according to your order, you have created the Crisis Staff in Samac, would you agree with me then?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put to you that the TO as a component of the armed forces of the JNA was part of the armed forces of the JNA would you agree with me then?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence, the TO? No. The Territorial Defence was a component of the armed forces of the SFRY and it was under the command of the republic staffs of the TO but the JNA never had units of the TO. The JNA, during the combat activities, according to our military doctrine could have done tasks for the units of the TO but that was when the greater Yugoslavia existed, when Yugoslavia existed as a whole, when it got dismantled they no longer existed in such a way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put to you that in the month of April, up until the 19th of May, the TO for the area of responsibility covered by the 17th Tactical Group was under your command, would you agree with me then?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. I can only agree with one thing is that I had engaged some of the units of the TO who were belonging to the TO of the Serb republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put to you that the police was also a part and was under your area of responsibility and under you, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. I was never -- I never had the authority, any legal authority, over the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then would you agree with a portion of the interview that was given by Simo Zaric on Novi Sad television when he says that the 4th Detachment of the TO was preparing for attacking Samac and that it carried out that mission, would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, because the expression is not correct. And I would like you to give me a minute so that I can explain this. Whenever somebody hears a detachment, everybody knows or thinks TO. That was a habit and even my commander said or even the person who was working for me would write down TO as soon as one would hear detachment. The 4th Detachment was not a detachment of the TO but it was the detachment of the JNA precisely in order not to make any ambiguities because TO was organised at the republic level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put to you that you were responsible as a commander of a military unit for the fact that you did not press charges against Lugar who killed people in Crkvina on the 8th of May, 1992, would you agree with me then?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, I do not agree with you, but I can only declare the following. My command knew everything, I reported it to them, and later on, everything I told them was used in the trial against the gentleman that you've mentioned in Banja Luka. I don't know what the outcome of this was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that as a commander of an important military unit such as the 17th Tactical Group, you did not do everything in your power to arrest and to detain people, authors of the crime, authors of crimes who were conducted by these people in your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No I do not agree with you because my authority was only to declare that -- was only -- I was only competent if the state of war was proclaimed, the taking over the people from Bosanski Samac and the transferring of these people outside of my area of responsibility was legal [as interpreted]. I am -- I did this for humanitarian reasons and I will answer for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's it, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour there is something in the transcript that was not recorded what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Here. On page 65, line 22. The witness literally said even that was illegal but I did it. And here it says it was legal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps the witness can --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, can I go over that with the witness, Your Honour, this particular part of his statement?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, Mr. Nikolic, could you please tell us even if the transferring of people from Samac was what? What did you say, for the transcript?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In order for everything to be absolutely clear, after the conversation I had with the commander of the 17th Corps who very clearly said to me do everything in your power so that there is no conflict, that these people should be taken from Samac and should be transferred outside of your area of responsibility and these people would be sent to prisons or other detention centres, I did this. I agreed, and in fact, I did not have the authority to do this, and my commander, the corps commander, did not also have the right to order me the following -- that following order. We did this only to protect these people in order to protect them, not to have them under the attack. If I am guilty of this, well, I will then agree. And that's why I'm sitting here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I've finished with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What about this document with the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, maybe we could have ID, since I have to -- it speaks for itself but I will ask for the official translation so up to now maybe, up to then maybe we could have the ID number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be treated as document D181/1 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, the Prosecution? Cross-examined by Mr. Re:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, there, Mr. Nikolic. I have some questions to ask you for the Prosecution. A moment ago you just spoke about the trial in Banja Luka. That was of Crni, wasn't it, just yes or no?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I am not sure who was involved in that trial, all of the people who were involved but I know that the above-mentioned person was also on trial and Mirko Lugar was one of the people amongst other people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I ask to you answer something yes or no as to whether or not Crni was involved please just answer yes or no, I'm just after very specific information, please. Look the trial in Banja Luka that was to do with the -- please, let me finish the question.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if you don't know, how could you know that the information you gave was used against them in the trial? Which is the evidence you gave a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I found that out later, because that trial took place after I left Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm unclear. Can you please tell the Trial Chamber do you know what the trial concerned? Firstly, yes or no, if yes, I'll ask you what, if no, we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if I tell you it had nothing to do with the Crkvina massacre that would be a revelation for you, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yeah, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If it had nothing to do with the Crkvina massacre the information you passed on couldn't have been used, could it, sir? It's a matter of logic.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I said what I wrote down and whom I sent that information and I was expecting this information to be served in the Court of law and serve the purposes of justice. Now, I don't know if they used that information that I gave or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in your evidence earlier, you gave evidence of clashes between forces from the Republic of Croatia and troops from the JNA. To be quite clear, that was the army of the Republic of Croatia and the HVO combined, which were fighting the JNA forces in your area of responsibility, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was of course after the declaration by Croatia of independence from Yugoslavia in 1991, recognised in early 1992, wasn't it? What I'm saying is that between January and May when you left Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It's too fast. Your question was interpreted to me too quickly. If I understood you correctly you're asking me when did this take place, what period did it cover? These clashes became even greater and I said it started at the end of March and they lasted up until I left Bosnia up until the 19th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The defendant over there, Mr. Miroslav Tadic, you know him, don't you?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew him because he was among other things the assistant commander for logistics in the 4th Detachment which was ultimately under your command? Didn't you?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you known Mr. Tadic for?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot give you the exact figure but let's say after I arrived and after the tactical group was formed, that was on the 17th so up until the end of October so from the month of October, 1991 and on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, how long have you known Mr. Zaric for, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I met both of them at approximately the same time, with a small difference in -- concerning the time period but I probably met them at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying you met Mr. Zaric for the first time in October 1991, just to be clear, that's what you're saying, around that time?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the exact date. The tactical group was formed or I started working at the formation of the tactical group around that date but I cannot give you the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps it would really assist if you would listen very carefully to the question and answer it as precisely as possible. The question I asked you was: Was it around that date? Doesn't really require an explanation. I'm only interested in approximately. Now, I'll move on the question I want to ask you is: Would you consider yourself a friend of Mr. Zaric's or Mr. Tadic's, from the time you first met them?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I would say it differently. I am a man who recognises what they did and who respects what they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you respect about what Mr. Tadic did, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: To begin with, the time when they accepted the soldiers who were running away from Croatia up until the time when they were saved and then later on, from what happened to the 4th Detachment, I'd say that I would respect them or I would assess their work very positively.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course you're aware of Mr. Tadic's role as the head of the exchanges in Bosanski Samac for some period, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you're asking this question or if one is asking this question, we should also ask about the time. We know that the witness left around the 20th of May and we know that the first exchange took place on the 21st of May, 26th of May, so if we are asking this question, we should ask the question about the involvement of Tadic during these exchanges.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The answer the witness gave which prompted me to ask that question was I am a man who recognises what they did and who respects what they did. That's a very open answer. He didn't say it was confined to a certain period. I'm just asking him what he knows and what he respects. Whether it be before he left the territory or afterwards. He knows or he doesn't. Why did he say that? What does he respect about them? I can divide the question into three but it will take longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think Mr. Lukic's concern was maybe he thought ahead that you are going to discuss what Mr. Miroslav Tadic was doing in connection with exchanges. That's why he was particular about time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour my question was, you're aware of Mr. Tadic's role of the head of the exchanges in Bosanski Samac for some period, aren't you? The witness hasn't answered whether he knows Mr. Tadic's role. When doesn't really matter. I just want to know whether he was aware of Mr. Tadic's role in exchanges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You understand that Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... you are you were aware of Mr. Tadic's role as chairman of the exchange commission, were you?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That role, I am not aware of that. I knew that he was involved and I knew what he was doing only when I was his commander, at the time he was doing what he was to do, as an assistant for logistics in the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your respect for his contribution is confined to his job as assistant commander for logistics before you left the territory, is that so?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's correct. And then it would not go further because I have no idea what else was done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What about Dr. Blagoje Simic? When did you first meet Dr. Simic, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall with precision, but I believe that I met Mr. Blagoje Simic sometime in the month of December, maybe, 1991, sometime around that date, but I couldn't really give you a precise date.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's 12.30, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we will take our break and continue afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re, you're continuing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, your evidence earlier to Mr. Pisarevic was of you having some contact with Mr. Todorovic and Dr. Simic before the takeover on the 16th and 17th of April, 1992. This is just an introductory question. You remember that evidence? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I spoke to them many times. I don't know whether we talked before the 16th and 17th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please listen very carefully to my question? And only answer that and not another one? It will be much quicker for all of us if we do it this way. What I want to ask you about is the contact you had with Mr. Todorovic and Dr. Simic. Firstly, were you present at the meeting establishing the Serbian Municipality of Samac on the 29th of February, 1992?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present at the meeting on the 28th of March, 1992 -- sorry, 1992, in Obudovac in relation to the appointment of the executive council and officers of the Serbian Municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you send a representative to either of these meetings to attend on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Colonel Mico Djurdjevic went to one meeting but I don't know exactly which one. I mean out of those that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But Colonel, when Colonel Mico Djurdjevic went, was it as your representative or a representative of the JNA or the 4th Detachment or the 17th Tactical Group? In what capacity was he there?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly now which meeting this was, but if he went to this meeting, he went as a representative of the 17th Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Third meeting I wish to ask you about is the meeting at which the Crisis Staff was formed in St. Sava hall in Obudovac on the 15th of April, 1992. Did you attend this meeting yourself or did a representative of the JNA or the 17th Tactical Group attend that meeting, that's the formation of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I did not attend it, and I did not send a representative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You first met Dr. Simic in -- sorry you said I think in December, 1991, and your evidence a little bit later was that you had talked to him many times. I just want to ask you approximately, I'm not trying to pin you down to a number, how often did you or how many times did you speak to him between when you first met him and the takeover on the 17th of April, when he telephoned you at 3.00 a.m. In the morning?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps six or seven times. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you communicate with him after the formation of the Serbian Municipality of Samac in his official capacity as the head of that -- or the chairman or the president of that municipality? That's between the 29th of February, 1992 -- I'll just finish it -- and the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, unless there is an evidence with regard to the capacity of Dr. Blagoje Simic as a chairman, I think it's a little bit confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll withdraw the question in that form. It was my confusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you communicate with Dr. Blagoje Simic between December -- I'm sorry, between the 29th of February, 1992 and the 17th of April, 1992, in his capacity as the local president of the SDS and his activities connected with the Samac municipality, Serbian municipality?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I did not have any contacts with him as with a representative of the SDS but I did have contacts with him in his capacity of president of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the Serbian municipality before the takeover, to be quite clear?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Before the takeover and after the takeover, I had contacts with him. Before the takeover I contacted with him as with Blagoje Simic, a particular personality, and after the takeover he was president of the municipality. I had to contact with people, those who held certain offices, I had no other way to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, please be precise. My question was only confined to before the takeover. Likewise, your evidence earlier was that you had contact with Mr. Todorovic. Now, Mr. Todorovic was appointed as the chief of police of the -- or chief of the public security station of the Serbian Municipality of Samac on the 28th of March, 1992. Between that date, when he was appointed the chief of public security station and the takeover on the 17th of April, 1992, what communication -- sorry, did you communicate with him in his capacity as the chief of the public security station?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: First of all, I did not know at all when he was appointed chief of the public security station. I communicated with him as with Stevan Todorovic, in his personal capacity. When he introduced himself and when he said that he was appointed municipal chief of security, then I contacted with him as with head of the public security station because I was resolving certain problems and I explained a while ago what kind of contacts these were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm trying to ask you about is before the takeover. You were aware that he had -- or he had been appointed as the chief of the police of the Serbian Municipality of Samac before the takeover, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. If you wish to have a full answer, I knew that when they took over the municipality and when Todorovic said that he was head of the station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Todorovic was before the 17th of April, working in a wicker factory, a factory that made baskets. Why were you communicating with him before the takeover in his capacity as Stevan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I think that God all mighty himself cannot give an answer to that question. He was simply after me all the time and wanted to talk to me, whenever any kind of occasion arose, he chased me, asked me questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just excuse me for one moment? I'm just trying to find something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were of course aware that a democratically elected government was supposed to be in power in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, having been elected in October, 1990, as of April, 1992, weren't you, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I was not sent either to appoint or dismiss governments. I was sent to carry out a combat assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask my question again and please answer the question I'm asking you. The question was: You were aware in April 1992, weren't you, that there was a democratically elected government which was supposed to be in power in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I knew that there was that government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already told us you knew that Dr. Simic was connected with the Serbian municipality, and that this Serbian municipality had proclaimed itself at the same time?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection. We didn't hear that he said that Dr. Blagoje Simic was connected with Serbian municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't have the transcript in front of me. I can try and locate it. It will take me a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Perhaps -- yes, perhaps it will help, Mr. Re, if you're specific instead of using the word "connected."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did ask a question earlier, I'm searching for the answer he gave. I can't find it on the lap top to my left. Maybe it's on the lap top to my right, if I can just have a moment to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour in the meantime maybe I can be of assistance, it is not in dispute in this case that Dr. Blagoje Simic was elected in election of 1990 as a vice-president, vice-chairman of the municipal assembly of Bosanski Samac. And he was on the same position until the 17th of April, 1992, when he became president, allegedly, in this period of president of Crisis Staff, Serbian municipality but he never was president of Serbian municipality, information or any other function.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, I withdrew that question. I asked another question. The question was: Did you communicate with Dr. Simic between -- in his capacity as the local president of the SDS and his activities connected with the Samac municipality, to which the answer was: I did not have any contacts with him as a representative of the SDS but I did have contacts with him in his capacity as president of the municipality. It's on the record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could take you back to my question sir, and the question I was going to ask you --

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That was not the answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about your contact with Dr. Simic before the takeover on the 17th of April, 1992. We've already established that there was a democratically elected government in power. And a Serbian municipality had proclaimed itself. Now of course you're aware that this Serbian municipality which proclaimed itself was one which concentrated power in the hands of Serbs only and that non-Serbs could not participate as elected representatives of the municipality which was covering an area which had a non-Serb majority. You're aware of that, aren't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, the proclamation of a Serbian municipality and the takeover of power by Serbs to the exclusion of the non-Serbs wouldn't exactly promote interethnic harmony, would it, sir?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Are you asking me for my opinion?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were there, sir.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I was there but I'm not an expert. If you're asking me, I can have an opinion of my own. I believe that there can be no harmony if only one people governs, if only one ethnic group governs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, sir, and it could lead to, sorry, the usurping of power by one ethnicity at the expense of the others could lead to ethnic clashes, couldn't it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And given the extremely delicate nature of interethnic relations in Bosnia-Herzegovina in the first half of 1992, you would agree, wouldn't you, that such a takeover by the Serbs would result in ethnic clashes because of what had been occurring in other parts of Bosnia, wouldn't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I was there precisely to prevent that kind of interethnic conflict, and where this led to can be seen from what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in your statement, you said that the mission or the task of the 17th Tactical Group was to, among other things, prevent the outbreak of ethnic clashes in the tactical group's area, sorry, zone of responsibility. Of course --

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Allowing the Serbian -- or the Serbs to take over the municipality at the expense of the non-Serbs breached that fundamental task or objective or mission of the 17th Tactical Group, didn't it? That is to prevent the outbreak of ethnic clashes, because ethnic clashes occurred as a result of the takeover, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe it's a call for speculation. I mean what was the reason for clashes, whether they would appear because of the takeover or for some other reasons, we have also evidence that there were arming between parties and.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Realtime transcript read in error "MR. LAZAREVIC:"] Stop, stop, you cannot do that. You cannot clue the witness. You can object but not do that. I press the question on the basis that the witness was there and was charged with "preventing the outbreak of the ethnic clashes in the tactical group's zone of responsibility," paragraph 14 of his statement in evidence here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the witness can answer. Except that in the transcript, there is no separation from Mr. Lazarevic's objection and after the time you start talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I hope it will be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic has indicated he objected to his own question which wasn't the case. That will be corrected in the transcript --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question, Mr. Nikolic, was allowing the Serbs to take over the municipality at the expense of the non-Serbs it breached the fundamental mission or objective of the 17th Tactical Group, that is to prevent the outbreak of ethnic clashes because ethnic clashes did in fact occur as a result of the takeover, from which you saw, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Allow me to explain this. I believe that things cannot be put that way because the 17th Tactical Group was not the one who was supposed to regulate who will and when and where take over government, and plan government, et cetera. My task was to prevent the killing of people, prevent the possibility of interethnic conflicts breaking out, et cetera. As I already said a while ago, everybody created Crisis Staffs, everybody had units of their own, everybody wanted to be the one that's going to be in power. Then it would seem that I was supposed to take the tactical group and start attacking everyone and that would have been senseless.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you cannot disagree with me, can you, that what happened on the 17th of April, 1992, was a military takeover by Serbs and Serb forces of a democratically elected government and all the instrumentalities of government, you can't disagree with that, can you?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I have agreed with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the extent of your communications with Dr. Simic before the takeover, how often you spoke to him and what you spoke to him about in the period leading up to the 17th of April when you received that telephone call at 3.00 a.m. in the morning?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I can say to you that he and Mr. Todorovic often wanted to talk to me. They were particularly interested in the assignments of the tactical group, what the army was doing, et cetera. I have the impression that they saw me as a communist officer who they did not trust very much. For them, after all, I was Tito's officer. Therefore, their attitude towards me was a sceptical one. I often had the impression that they were trying to keep me under some kind of control. Why? They know that the best. I did not allow that. And I did my job professionally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of things did Dr. Simic say to you when he contacted you or communicated with you in the months prior to the takeover on the 17th of August -- sorry, April?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, various things were discussed, attempts were made to discuss politics, possible events, possible developments, I said that I was not interested in that, I was given a task that I had to carry out and that is the only thing that I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it you contacting him or him contacting you?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: For the most part, he contacted me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the other part, when you contacted him -- maybe there is a misunderstanding here. You said for the most part, meaning he mostly contacted you. When you contacted him, what did you contact him about? How many times did you contact him before the takeover and why did you contact him?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There weren't any reasons for me to contact him before the takeover. For the most part he and Todorovic came to me, and they tried in different ways to find out what was going on, they tried to collect information, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what capacity was he contacting you, Dr. Simic, local medical practitioner, in what capacity was he, Dr. Simic, contacting you? The head of the local JNA?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I have to say to you that you obviously do not understand the Serb mentality. Every day I had 50 people who came to see me, to ask me about something, to see what was going on. That is an approach that is quite unbelievable and it took a lot of my time and that is how these contacts took place as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your evidence earlier to Mr. Pisarevic was that you put observers on the silos. Now, these observers, I take it, were armed, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. All members of the tactical group, of Tactical Group 17, were armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they armed with sniper rifles, the ones who were on the silos?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, no. The silo is sufficiently far away. I mean it was used as an observation point, because -- if you understand what I'm saying, because it rises so high then one could observe from there even without optical instruments what was going on and even what was going on on the other side of the Sava River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, was it on the 17th, the morning of the 17th of April, that you placed people, placed your men, on the silos using it as an observation post?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We already have the answer to that, if my colleague was reading this carefully, he said after this -- after the 4th Detachment was raised, his combat readiness. It is in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm only after the date. If I've missed it, I apologise. I'm just after the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, go on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it on the 17th, the morning of the 17th, that you placed those people in the silos?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. I placed people on the silo on the 17th, sometime in the afternoon, when there was already a danger of forces from Croatia crossing over to the Bosnian side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already agreed with me that it was a military takeover of the municipality by the Serbs. Now that of course would qualify in your own understanding as an armed insurrection against legitimate organs of government, wouldn't it, at least on a local level?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Probably, yes, but that is why there were organs of authority at republican level that were supposed to take certain measures. It is well known who is accountable to who.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had intelligence information and reliable intelligence information at the time, that members of the 1st Detachment under your command, that's Stevan Todorovic and Mijak Ivanovic, participated in the takeover, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. But Todorovic had already been replaced and as for Mijak, we got this information much later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say much later, what's much later, Mr. Nikolic? Before you left Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, say, I think, no, no, no. No. Well, I still was in Bosnia but after that, he was relieved and another man was appointed, and he went to become a TO commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll just take you back a step. You've already agreed that I think you said probably it would amount to an armed insurrection, which of course as you know was illegal under federal Yugoslavian code, you had information that at least one member, a commander of one of your detachments had participated in an armed insurrection. You found out about that a bit later. You found out about that when you were still the commander, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Look, I can't now pinpoint the time when that was established, all I know is that from the Secretariat, the information arrived that he was being transferred to another position and that another man was being appointed to his post but I can't give you the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the commander, what steps, if any, did you take to ensure that this person, Ivanovic, who participated in at least the preemptive strike or the preemptive planning of the takeover of Bosanski Samac, if not on the day, what actions did you take to ensure he was brought to justice for his illegal activities?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Look, those illegal activities, if they indeed existed, became obvious only after my departure so that there was nothing in particular that I could do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your evidence to Mr. Pisarevic or I think maybe it was Mr. Pantelic, was that you used police in some of your military activities. I don't think it's in your statement there. You said it earlier this morning. Were these regular police? I just want to ask you about regular police from the --

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I remember that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to ask you, please confine yourself to regular police, that's not the paramilitaries, regular police from the Samac police station. I want you to tell the Trial Chamber when you used these police and what you used them for, how you managed to obtain these police to help you on the front line.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The Tactical Group 17 was surrounded, and sometime between the 7th to the 10th of May, certain problems had to be resolved because the road from Brcko towards Loncari and Orasje was blocked and likewise the road which from Samac goes to Modrica. Since the attacks of the forces from Croatia were considerable and engaged all my units, then in the villages, I collected those small detachments which by that time had already become TO detachments, sent a request to my corps commander to establish contact with relevant authorities, and to have Todorovic informed that I was being authorised to engage the police, and about 40 to 45 policemen were taken on and that is how we carried out those operations, that is unblocking the roads in both directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was only asking you about regular police from the Samac police station. You used both on the actions between the 7th and 10th of May to clear the roads towards Modrica and towards Brcko; is that correct -- Orasje, sorry, Brcko?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's right. All the policemen that I could get.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these police of course were subordinated to you for that period of time, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Look, at the time, when the task was being carried out, when the communication between the civilian authorities and my corps command which was responsible for this was established, then these policemen were attached, that is resubordinated to me, for a while. After that period elapsed, it was my duty to return them to let them go back to their police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were the commanding officer in relation to the clearing of the road to Brcko and Modrica between the 7th and the 10th of May, and all troops involved in that were subordinated to you, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When you say all troops, then you must understand that the overwhelming majority of forces were already engaged on the right bank of the Sava and on the right bank of the Bosna River, in fighting members of the Croatian formations and the forces of the Croat Defence Council. So at that time, I no longer had any forces at my disposal. I was simply trying to get every man I could get, in order to put together units which could clear those roads and ensure normal communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were the officer who issued the order for the clearing of those two roads, weren't you, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yeah. I never gave any orders to cleanse the roads. My only order to the units was to take steps when the roads were blocked, to make the enemy pull away from those roads so that normal communication could be re-established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You issued orders on the 7th of May in relation to the unblocking or clearing of the roads in the area of Modrica on one side and Brcko on the other over the next three days, didn't you, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I issued one order for -- to free the communication towards Modrica because that was the task I got from my commander and my second order was to liberate the communication from Loncari towards Brcko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In issuing those orders, you drew up battle plans subordinating various units, coordinating them to do the two separate tasks, didn't you, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The plans for the execution of these tasks were drawn at the Tactical Group 17 and were carried out as such. Except that the plan concerning Modrica when the attack started a commander of a paramilitary unit, some Perija, had already fled, and the road had already been cleared so that that attack never would -- would never really got in full swing, never was completed, I mean it was finished. It was all over by around 10.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You issued orders for the subordination -- of the attack in which various units were subordinated to your command for those two areas, Modrica and Brcko over those three days, didn't you? You were the commanding officer, the units you issued the orders to were subordinated to you for that period, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Correct, so I issued the orders and I commanded them during the execution of the task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, of course, two of those groups included battalions headed by Crni and Lugar, didn't they, sir?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: This is how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lugar and Crni headed two of the groups that you issued orders to between the 7th and the 10th of May, correct? Easy question.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, the question is simple but the answer isn't and I must give you a precise answer. Since the crime in Crkvina happened between the 8th and the 9th, this order was issued -- was written on the 7th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about Crkvina. I'm asking you only about the issuing of the orders and I'm going to show you two orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the usher please show these two orders to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Do you have exhibit numbers, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No. They are not in evidence at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Not yet.
