utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please put them on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, look, I just want to say to you if you have some difficulties, if you feel that answering a question may incriminate you, the Trial Chamber will warn you and specifically in relation to command responsibility, and Article 21 of the document Mr. Pantelic referred to you which is D179/1, and if my questions suggest to you that you were in charge of those troops at the time the Crkvina massacre was committed and that you as a commanding officer based on those orders had a duty to punish or prevent, and if the answer you give based on those documents, incriminates you, you have a right to object and the Trial Chamber may direct you to answer the question. I'm just alerting the Trial Chamber to that at this very moment, based on those orders. So can you please look at the two orders, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and just one -- to be fair to the witness, he asked to explain. It is really unfair because this is a situation that my colleague is referring to, and I believe that the witness has the right to give a full explanation of these documents that have just been tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I won't interfere with the witness's right to give a full explanation. I want to ask him about the two orders which on their face subordinate Lugar and Crni's units to him for those two attacks. This is corroborated by other evidence before the Trial Chamber, specifically P127.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't understand, Mr. Lazarevic, because the witness is given the documents and he can answer the questions according to the way he understands them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I just wanted the witness not to be interrupted in giving his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: His answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Because he cannot simply answer yes or no when he looks at the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, of course, the witness will be allowed to give his answers as complete as he wishes them to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Firstly, sir, can you please look at the document, the two documents I have given you? Which one have you put on the ELMO there?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I've put the one which says, "Command, the left column."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the page, you'll see it's the 7th of May, 1992, and it is a two page document?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Document that you've signed, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's an order for units to be ready to attack on the 10th of May, 1992, in the direction of Modrica, isn't it? That's what you've just given the evidence about?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Not on the 10th. This is the order about the preparedness for attack on the 8th at 6.00 and it seems that we've put wrong documents on. I put the document number 2 and you put document number 1. Do you want me to put on document number 1? Here it is in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please put it on the screen and if you could just possibly turn to your side so that everyone, the interpreters and everyone can see the order? Right. This is the one for the attack on the 10th of May, 1992, again this is also an order you issued with your signature on it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's right but let me explain what this is about. If I may, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a moment, sir, you'll have a full chance in a moment. I just want to ask you a few questions first. If you look at the text of the document it's got the words Lugar written in large letters on the top right of the front page. Is that your handwriting, sir?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, it isn't. This is the handwriting of somebody in the staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you look at the body of the text, number 1, which is about halfway down the first page, it says, "A north column composed of the Lugar group and Territorial Defence company enforced with Praga platoon from the second battery shall carry out the attack in the direction of Milosevac village, Obalj [phoen], Garevac village, Modrica." And so on. If you go down further it's supported by 128 millimetre mortar battery and 82 millimetre mortar platoon. You can see that, can't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I see it everything, and I know this order by heart, literally. May I explain?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not yet, not yet. You will have your chance. If you go down, you will see that the words, "Commander of column, Lugar." Lugar is in inverted commas. That clearly indicates that Lugar was the commander of one of the units, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That shows that he was supposed to be one of the commanders of the columns but it doesn't show that he was because this document should be accompanied by other documents. There is a supplement to the order for this task in which the actors were changed, and they were changed after the crime in Crkvina, and that is what I'm trying to explain to you but you're not letting me to do that. So we have a different situation now, because the crime happened, I removed certain people. For instance the commander of the south column, the third one, it says, Crni, and yet it was Major Zoran Jovanovic, and the first one, war it says Lugar was as a matter of fact Srecko Radovanovic, Debeli. That is what I'm trying to tell you. So I took steps to remove those people from there. But if documents are being shown, then all the documents need to be shown, documents cannot be taken out of the context. This is only one of the orders and it shows when it was planned, it shows that there is a time, objectively, during when I established all the contacts with my superior command and Mr. Stevan Todorovic when he was ordered to resubordinate the policemen to me for this task, he insisted that some of his men, if at all possible, to have some of his men appointed commanders of the columns and I told him where that could be done and where that could not be done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could just take you back to the document, sir, if you turn over the page, it refers to the third column, the commander of that column was Crni, doesn't it? That's what it says. This was on the 7th of May, you issued the order for Lugar's men and Crni's men to take part in an attack and to be subordinated to your command for that period, wasn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. On the 7th, the preparations were done. The date up here shows when was the preparation done, and when the document was done. The document is delivered to those who are supposed to carry it out and it is made more precise by previous order which you should have shown me, when are -- which units to report, and to be subordinated to the commander of the Tactical Group 17. So they reported immediately before the task and as soon as the task would be over, they would be relieved of their duty and sent back to perform their law enforcement jobs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could just take you to the second document you have there, also dated the 7th of May, 1992, if you could just turn to your right to have a look at that, that's dated the same day, you've already agreed it has your signature on it. It again, about halfway down the page, in relation to the attack in the general direction of Markovic Polja, Grabovica [phoen], Brcko, refers to the use of the Lugar group, doesn't it? That's 2.1.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That is correct, yes. That is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was for according to this, an attack on the -- according to your evidence an attack on the 8th of May, wasn't it, 6.00 a.m. on the 8th of April, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's right. That is the attack which --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the date? And according to your evidence, you didn't hear about the Crkvina massacre until the 9th of May, did you? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just asked you about the date?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I thought your evidence earlier was that Mr. Mr. Zaric told you about the Crkvina massacre on the 9th, the morning of the 9th.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That is correct. The massacre happened between the 8th and the 9th. In the afternoon and in the morning of the 9th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course according to these -- according to these attack plans the attack was supposed to occur on the 8th of April, first thing in the morning, that is the day before or long before or hours before the Crkvina massacre wasn't it? Wasn't it? According to the face of this document. Yeah?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We started the attack as planned. The attack was over at 11.00 in the morning. The road was unblocked and around 12.00 already or perhaps even earlier, all those who had been incorporated in the Tactical Group 17 as temporary reinforcement had already been released and sent back to their usual jobs. That is what I'm trying to explain to you, and then in the next document, when this happened, I simply eliminated them, wrote another order, and engaged other individuals. That is what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see, sir. So you're saying that you actually used Lugar and his men on the 8th up until about mid-day, and then let them go home; is that right? Even though you're other order said they were to be used on the 10th as well, you let them go after using them on the 8th? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That is what I'm trying to tell you because they had nothing to do for me. They were performing their law enforcement jobs and I had to just borrow them while I needed them. Otherwise, they were in the police. And you keep talking about Lugar or this or that but I'm talking about policemen, about law enforcement officers in the police station in Bosanski Samac, and I engaged everybody that I could lay my hands on in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the order says, this is the first one, about the attack, was 100 men from the special detachment of the Lugar group, with an 82 millimetre mortar platoon and 60 millimetre mortar squad, Praga platoon, the command of the column Crni. Those are the troops you used on the 8th of May, Lugar and 100 men from his special detachment. It doesn't say local police, does it, sir? Does it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, not the local police, when they report to me and when they are attached to me, then in the order will not mention them as the local police. Once the task is over I turn them back to their regular jobs. So that in this particular case, there was Lugar and some men from the special detachment and I just explained it a moment ago that in the motorised battalion, the first motorised battalion, a company of 60, 70 men had been specially trained for active operations, and he was given some of them to carry out the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May the documents be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise to my learned friend. Sorry, sorry, Your Honour. It's just a clarification, if you're looking at this document which is on the ELMO, let's clarify that with the witness, it's just a suggestion, we have a date 8 of April which is absolutely inconsistent with the top left-hand side. Obviously it's an error in writing. So maybe we could clarify that although the testimony is very clear of this witness but still, for the sake of transcript. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Certainly but may the documents be tendered into evidence at this point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, can we have the explanation first?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you can see that it does say the 8th in handwritten letter, the 8th of April, on the document headed "lijeva kolona." That's the one the 8th of April -- the 8th of May you just explained to us where Lugar and Crni were involved in the clearing or the operations in Brcko, it says the 8th of April, that's clearly a mistake isn't it? It clearly is meant to be the 8th of May, from your evidence just then, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can explain that. This is a mistake here. Somebody in the staff made this mistake because he should have written the 8th of -- the 5th month, May. That is one thing. Secondly, in the army, you have so-called preceding orders, regulating which units will be subordinated to whom, report to whom, how it will be prepared and so on and so forth, so they were taken over on the eve of the attack. We started the attack towards Brcko because the Croatian units had taken the village of Grebnica, in front of us we have Perry Colton, an American, whom we captured as a member of the first Brigade of the ZNG and who had destroyed the bridge across the Tinja. Tinja was crossed these from Grebnica pulled out and all there was over by, say, around 10.00 that day. Around 11.00, I sent those people off and I said, you go back to your jobs. And that was then followed or rather there was already a plan prepared for the attack towards Modrica. And the grouping is done when the task is about to be carried out. And that is the principal matter because it shows if you group people earlier then it becomes common knowledge, the moment you've grouped your people together the enemy already knows that they are there together and what they are about to do. So that when this was done, there was no crime, but there was a communication and there was an order to Todorovic that he had to attach his police and that solved the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There was a request to admit. Is there any objection from the Defence? None at all. Can we have the number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The order with ERN number 0063-6931 will be marked as document P174 ter ID. The order with the ERN number 0063-6932 will be marked as document P175 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We don't have English translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Don't we? We should have. Certainly Mr. Leese has photocopied them all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So they should be admitted as exhibits, not just marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, they will be exhibits P174 ter and P174, and P175 ter and P175.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. We shall adjourn and continue our proceedings tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 1.51 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 15th day of April, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
